transcript: So I finally saw Here We Are, Sondheim’s last musical, and this one seems to be divisive. A lot of people love it, a lot of people don't like it, and I unfortunately was more towards the don't like it side. As always I will start with the positives, I think the cast is phenomenal and everyone is giving incredible performances. It is truly just a stacked cast, and I spent a good chunk of the show just staring in awe being like I cannot believe I'm watching all of these actors on stage together right now. I thought the show was really funny, and I think that if you like surrealist stuff you're going to enjoy the show a lot more than if you're someone who does not like surrealist. But overall I did find it be pretty engaging, particularly Act 1. Act 2 I did think lost some steam but it's also the act with less music, so maybe that's why. Which, let's talk about the music… because while I do think the music that we have is very good, I was a little bit disappointed that there wasn't more of it. There are a good number of songs in Act 1, but I wouldn't say a lot, and then in Act 2 there's like the first 10 minutes are sung through and then there's no more music for the rest of the act (at least music with lyrics). There are a few moments of underscoring in Act 2, and for most of those moments it kind of felt like they were almost earmarked to be songs at some point, and obviously with Sondheim passing away he was never able to actually write songs for those moments, but there were several moments in Act 2 that I felt like could have really benefited from having a song and that would have really enhanced the material. I also don't really think that Sondheim necessarily brought anything new to the table with the score. It all felt like a lot of melodies that we've heard from him before, or derivative of some of his other work. And the other thing that I think really hurts the score is there's no big soaring number that really brings it home. There's no Move On. There's no Being Alive. There's no No More. And because of that, I just found myself wanting a little bit more out of the score even though I know that's a little bit out of their hands. The show itself is very weird, very surreal, your mileage will vary. But as someone who doesn't particularly love surreal theatre I did find the plot to be a little bit lacking and I struggled with what the text really wanted us to take from it. But I am still glad this show exist, and I am glad I saw it. And if you're wondering if you should see it, honestly my answer is: If you're someone who wants to see all of the Sondheim shows I would recommend seeing this Because 1)  I don't know how often the show is going to be done after this production, 2) I don't think you are ever going to find a better production of this show, even if the show itself is just okay. Between this cast, the set and and the direction, which is fantastic!
